items.stem: During autoregressive LLM inference, which factor often dominates memory use for long contexts?

options.text: The KV cache that stores keys and values for all previous tokens
options.rationale: Correct: the KV cache grows with sequence length and dominates memory.
The vocabulary is small and fixed.
Learning rate is a training concept, not inference memory.
The seed does not consume meaningful memory.

items.explanation: Correct: the KV cache grows with sequence length and dominates memory.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about quantization are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Lower precision reduces memory and can speed up inference
options.rationale: Correct: smaller numeric types cut memory and bandwidth.

options.text: Aggressive quantization can degrade accuracy if sensitive layers are not handled
options.rationale: Correct: some layers need higher precision to preserve accuracy.
It typically trades some accuracy for efficiency.
Post-training quantization needs no full retraining.

items.explanation: Correct: smaller numeric types cut memory and bandwidth.
